Subject: Next steps & proposed trial onboarding plan — Magnolia AI

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion on the search-ranking use case and the latency targets you shared (~150ms p95). Quick recap and a proposed 3-week trial plan to validate throughput/quality and integration effort.

High-level recap:
- Primary success criteria: 1) end-to-end response latency <= 180ms p95; 2) model accuracy (nDCG@10) within 6% of current baseline; 3) integration work under 2 engineer-weeks.
- Scope: production-like query sampling + 10k synthetic queries, 1k real queries from your QA set, and basic scoring comparator.

Proposed trial / onboarding checkpoints (attachments: magnolia-poc-checklist.xlsx):
1) Week 0 (kickoff): access & creds, data ingestion spec, confirm sample dataset
2) Week 1: baseline capture, initial model + quantization profile, latency tuning
3) Week 2: run comparative evals, run throughput tests, refine batching/kv-caching
4) Week 3: handoff and success-review; decision meeting

Ownership:
- Redwood: technical onboarding, model hosting, infra tuning — Priyom Das (cc'd)
- Magnolia: dataset export + product owner — Aisha Patel
- Legal/Procurement: procurement@magnoliaai.com for contract/PO

Next steps / asks from your side:
- Confirm dataset delivery window (ETA: Apr 12)
- Confirm PO/procurement contact and timeline
- Share any non-functional requirements beyond latency (rate limits, retention)

I've attached a one-page checklist and a sample SLA for procurement. If this looks good I can convert to a mutual action plan in HubSpot and send calendar invites for the kickoff.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com
(415) 555-0192

Hi Aisha — quick tech note as requested.

Short answers:
- Token lengths: we saw median request ~25 tokens, 95th ~320 tokens in similar search queries; if your queries are similar, latency is dominated by context length and KV cache hits.
- Quantization: recommended starting point is 4-bit Q4/K-type where supported; it's a good balance for latency/cost. We can try Q8 first if you need more fidelity.
- Estimated trial burn (ballpark for 3 weeks): 250k tokens processed, ~120 GPU hours on an A10G-equivalent pool — approximate cost range $3,500–$7,000 depending on batching and cache effectiveness.

I'll prepare a 1-page tech appendix and drop it in the Drive link (see related links). For kickoff times, we have windows Mon/Wed mornings PST next week.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
